Extract environmental data some_sp <-   adm_extract(     data = some_sp,     x = "x",     y = "y",     env_layer = envar   )  # Fit some models mgam <- fit_abund_gam(   data = some_sp,   response = "ind_ha",   predictors = c("elevation", "sand", "bio3", "bio12"),   partition = ".part1",   distribution = "NO",   verbose = FALSE ) #> Formula used for model fitting: #> ind_ha ~ pb(elevation) + pb(sand) + pb(bio3) + pb(bio12) #> Warning: additive.fit convergence not obtained in  30  iterations  mraf <- fit_abund_raf(   data = some_sp,   response = "ind_ha",   predictors = c("elevation", "sand", "bio3", "bio12"),   partition = ".part1",   ntree = 100,   verbose = FALSE )  # adm_predict can be used for predict one or more models fitted with fit_ or tune_ functions  # a single model ind_p <- adm_predict(   models = mgam,   pred = envar,   training_data = some_sp,   nchunk = 1,   transform_negative = TRUE ) #> Predicting an individual model plot(ind_p$gam)   # a list of models list_p <- adm_predict(   models = list(mgam, mraf),   pred = envar,   training_data = some_sp,   nchunk = 1,   transform_negative = TRUE ) #> Predicting a list of models list_p #> $gam #> class       : SpatRaster #> size        : 201, 274, 1  (nrow, ncol, nlyr) #> resolution  : 0.08333333, 0.08333333  (x, y) #> extent      : -69.41681, -46.58347, -34.38347, -17.63347  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax) #> coord. ref. : lon/lat WGS 84 (EPSG:4326) #> source(s)   : memory #> varname     : envar #> name        :       gam #> min value   :         0 #> max value   : 44.503344 #>  #> $raf #> class       : SpatRaster #> size        : 201, 274, 1  (nrow, ncol, nlyr) #> resolution  : 0.08333333, 0.08333333  (x, y) #> extent      : -69.41681, -46.58347, -34.38347, -17.63347  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax) #> coord. ref. : lon/lat WGS 84 (EPSG:4326) #> source(s)   : memory #> varname     : envar #> name        :        raf #> min value   :          0 #> max value   : 148.743333 #>   # Predicting models in chunks helps reduce memory requirements in # cases where models are predicted for large scales and high resolution ind_p <- adm_predict(   models = mraf,   pred = envar,   training_data = some_sp,   nchunk = 4,   transform_negative = TRUE ) #> Predicting an individual model plot(ind_p$raf)  # }

title: Performs data transformation on a variable based on the specified method. — adm_transform
code: adm_transform(data, variable, method, inverse = FALSE, t_terms = NULL)

title: Performs data transformation on a variable based on the specified method. — adm_transform
text: data data.frame, tibble, SpatRaster containing data. variable character string specifying variable (column) transformed. method character string specifying method used transformation. Available methods "01", "zscore", "log", "round." "01", scales variable 0 1 using formula (x - min(x)) (max(x) - min(x)). "zscore", standardizes variable subtracting mean dividing standard deviation. "log", applies natural logarithm transformation variable. "log1", sums 1 applies natural logarithm transformation variable. "round", rounds variable's values nearest whole numbers. inverse logical. Invert transformation? t_terms vector. c(,b): "01", = min(x), b = max(x). "zscore", = mean(x), b = sd(x). "log" "log1, needed. invert "round" transformations.

title: Performs data transformation on a variable based on the specified method. — adm_transform
text: data.frame tibble transformed variable added new column. new column's name original variable name followed underscore method name.

walking 1 pixel at a time   conv_layers_padding = 1, # with 1 pixel of padding   number_of_fc_layers = 1, # followed by one fully connected layer   fc_layers_size = c(28), # with 28 neurons   pooling = NULL, # without average pooling   batch_norm = TRUE, # with batch normalization   dropout = 0 # and without dropout )  cnn_arch$net() # a torch net #> An `nn_module` containing 99,513 parameters. #>  #> ── Modules ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> • conv1: <nn_conv2d> #896 parameters #> • conv2: <nn_conv2d> #3,556 parameters #> • linear1: <nn_linear> #94,892 parameters #> • output: <nn_linear> #29 parameters #> • bn_conv1: <nn_batch_norm2d> #28 parameters #> • bn_conv2: <nn_batch_norm2d> #56 parameters #> • bn_linear1: <nn_batch_norm1d> #56 parameters cnn_arch$arch %>% cat() # the torch code to create it #> net <- torch::nn_module( #>   'conv_neural_net', #>   initialize = function() { #>     self$conv1<-torch::nn_conv2d(7,14,3,1,1) #>     self$conv2<-torch::nn_conv2d(14,28,3,1,1) #>     self$linear1<-torch::nn_linear(3388,28) #>     self$output<-torch::nn_linear(28,1) #>     self$bn_conv1<-torch::nn_batch_norm2d(num_features=14) #>     self$bn_conv2<-torch::nn_batch_norm2d(num_features=28) #>     self$bn_linear1<-torch::nn_batch_norm1d(num_features=28) #>   }, #>   forward = function(x) { #>     x %>% #>       self$conv1() %>% #>       torch::nnf_relu() %>% #>       self$bn_conv1() %>% #>       self$conv2() %>% #>       torch::nnf_relu() %>% #>       self$bn_conv2() %>% #>       torch::torch_flatten(start_dim = 2) %>% #>       self$linear1() %>% #>       torch::nnf_relu() %>% #>       self$bn_linear1() %>% #>       self$output() #>   } #> ) cnn_arch$arch_dict # and a quick description of its structure #> $`conv2-fc1-net` #>        [,1] #> conv_1   14 #> conv_2   28 #> fc_1     28 #>  # }

Fit some models mglm <- fit_abund_glm(   data = some_sp,   response = "ind_ha",   predictors = c("bio12", "elevation", "sand"),   predictors_f = c("eco"),   partition = ".part1",   distribution = "ZAIG",   poly = 3,   inter_order = 0,   predict_part = TRUE ) #> Formula used for model fitting: #> ind_ha ~ bio12 + elevation + sand + eco + I(bio12^2) + I(elevation^2) + I(sand^2) + I(bio12^3) + I(elevation^3) + I(sand^3) #> Replica number: 1/1 #> -- Partition number 1/3 #> -- Partition number 2/3 #> -- Partition number 3/3  # Partial Dependence Plots:  # In different resolutions p_abund_pdp(   model = mglm,   resolution = 50,   training_data = some_sp,   response_name = "Abundance" )   p_abund_pdp(   model = mglm,   resolution = 5,   training_data = some_sp,   response_name = "Abundance" )   # Especific variables and different resulotions p_abund_pdp(   model = mglm,   predictors = c("bio12", "sand"),   training_data = some_sp,   response_name = "Abundance" )   # With residuals and rug plot p_abund_pdp(   model = mglm,   training_data = some_sp,   response_name = "Abundance",   resid = TRUE )   p_abund_pdp(   model = mglm,   training_data = some_sp,   response_name = "Abundance",   rug = TRUE )   p_abund_pdp(   model = mglm,   training_data = some_sp,   response_name = "Abundance",   resid = TRUE,   rug = TRUE )   # Partial depence plot for training and projection condition found in a projection area p_abund_pdp(   model = mglm,   training_data = some_sp,   projection_data = envar,   response_name = "Abundance",   rug = TRUE )   # Custumize colors and theme p_abund_pdp(   model = mglm,   predictors = NULL,   resolution = 100,   resid = TRUE,   training_data = some_sp,   projection_data = envar,   colorl = c("blue", "red"),   colorp = "darkgray",   alpha = 0.4,   theme = ggplot2::theme_dark() )  # title: adm 0.5.0
text: title longer starts “Tools ”, Description now cites package paper (de Oliveira Junior Velazco 2025, doi:10.1111/2041-210X.70074). envar() cretusa_predictors() now return SpatRaster shipped package documented \value. Examples wrapped \donttest{} instead \dontrun{}; rewritten run, use declared dependencies, much faster (DNN/CNN examples run torch installed). function sets fixed random seed (set.seed(13), set.seed(ii) torch::torch_manual_seed(13) removed). Call set.seed() torch::torch_manual_seed() fitting need reproducible results. workflow vignette restores graphical parameters changes (par()). T replaced TRUE code examples.

title: adm 0.5.0
text: fit_abund_qrf now works partition used; calling internal result wrapper outdated argument order. Without partition now also returns predictors metadata, fit_abund_* functions . fit_abund_glm fit_abund_gam longer fail hold_out_set used (object 'train_set' found). fit_abund_net longer fails hold_out_set used (nnet predictions require type = "raw"). fit_abund_dnn now evaluates hold_out_set correctly longer builds mismatched default network predictors_f supplied (categorical predictors ignored, warning). fit_abund_cnn now works without partition; using hold_out_set CNN models now gives informative error yet supported. adm_predict now names predictions quantile regression forests qrf (named NA), p_abund_pdp/adm_predict longer rely $feature_names, recent xgboost versions provide. adm_uncertainty now accepts ... (documented), extra arguments needed CNN models (x, y, rasters, sample_size, custom_architecture) can passed.

title: adm 0.5.0
text: New tests fit_abund_* (algorithms, including -partition, hold-DNN/CNN paths), tune_abund_qrf, adm_transform (inverse raster), adm_predict, adm_uncertainty, model_selection, data_abund_pdp, p_abund_pdp, p_abund_bpdp, generate_dnn_architecture, generate_cnn_architecture, res_calculate, family_selector, croppin_hood, cnn_make_samples get_partition_samples. slow tune_abund_* tests (XGB one error checks), DNN/CNN prediction tests slowest data_abund_bpdp test skipped CRAN, vignette grids reduced, keep check time low.
